In social networks for instance, such as the one shown in Fig. 1 , the TLP task is to predict the likelihood of a future link between User 1 and User 3 based on the observed temporal interactions among users. Fig. 1 Temporal link prediction in a social network Recently, numerous methods have been proposed to address the TLP problem, each method focusing on different network characteristics. Solving TLP requires two key ingredients: first, a representation unit , which models how a temporal network can be captured to reflect its traits and historical dynamics; and second, an inference unit , which determines the likelihood of future links based on the learned representation. Since all TLP models necessarily need both units, this review is confined to approaches concerning either representation or inference. Traditional surveys often categorise TLP models into broad methodological families such as “learning-based” [ 11 ]. This perspective provides a useful overview of existing approaches, but tends to emphasise overall model families rather than disentangling specific design choices.
